description: Where the gameplay tuning numbers live in game/src, whether they are table-driven or literal, and whether they can become a data resource (MODDING.md R1/R2). Units: speeds are fx8.8 px/frame, timers are frames, hp/damage are hit points.

items.subject: enemies (types 0x00..0x37, plus items/projectiles)
items.what: starting hit points
items.notes: Already a manifest kind (obj_desc). Editing unk4 changes HP for every placement of the type. It also feeds the power of the star Kirby spits after inhaling (see kirby.spit_star_power) and is the heal amount for food items.

items.subject: all killable types
items.what: score awarded on kill
items.notes: obj_desc.unk2.

items.subject: enemies, some boss projectiles
items.what: copy ability granted on inhale

locations.note: ability statues: subtype1 -> ability via small C tables

items.notes: obj_desc.kirbyAbility covers most types; Golem (stone/wheel), Droppy (copies Kirby) and the statues override it in code.

items.subject: all objects
items.what: damage dealt to Kirby on contact (ObjectBase.unk63 = attack power)

locations.note: InitObject default: every enemy hits for 1
boss attack sub-objects set their own, almost always 1

items.notes: There is no per-type contact-damage table: InitObject hard-codes 1 and ~50 enemy/boss attack constructors set unk63 themselves. A data form would add a field to an obj_desc extension (or to a per-attack table).

items.subject: enemies + bosses (types 0x00..0x5C)
items.what: per-type damage modifier for each attack kind (resist/weakness): Object.unk91..unk96

locations.note: C const table, 6 x s8 per type
added to the attacker's unk63 when its unk68 has bit 0x100; result floored at 1

items.notes: Struct Unk_08352AD0 in game/include/data.h. Which unk68 attack bit maps to which column: 0x100->unk91, 0x200->unk92, 0x400->unk93, 0x1000->unk94, 0x4000->unk96, 0x2000->unk95, 0x40->unk94, 0x10000->unk97 (sub_0809AA10). Dark Mind overrides them with literals (-8/-32) in dark_mind.c. Good candidate for a new manifest kind next to obj_desc.

items.subject: all objects
items.what: hurt/hit rectangle (ObjectBase.unk38..unk3B) and terrain-collision bounds (unk3C..unk3F)

locations.note: per-constructor hit rect (left, top, right, bottom px)

items.notes: Each constructor calls sub_0803E2B0 / ObjectSetBounds with literals, often re-set per state (Waddle Dee 4x, Kirby attack objects ~90x). A per-type 'default hitbox' table could replace the constructor call; per-state changes stay in code.

items.subject: regular enemies
items.what: walk/fly speeds, jump impulses, turn timers
items.notes: Hard-coded in each behaviour state function. Moving them to data means a per-type parameter block and a code change in every enemy file; low value per effort except for a few showcase enemies.

items.subject: 24 enemy/boss files (Heavy Knight, Kracko, Foley, Droppy, Batty, ...)
items.what: keyframed motion: {xspeed, yspeed, xaccel, yaccel, frames, animSlot} steps

locations.note: unk8 = frames for this step; a 0 terminates

items.notes: Static const C arrays at fixed ROM addresses (named gUnk_0835xxxx). Each is a self-contained, terminated list: an easy 'motion_script' resource kind. Kirby also has one pointer of this type (Kirby.unk114, ROM table gUnk_08D6112C).

items.subject: all sprite objects
items.what: tile budget, palette, animation list
items.notes: obj_desc.numTiles / unk8 / unk14. Not gameplay tuning, but a mod that changes a sprite needs them.

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: max hp
items.notes: 6 + vitality pickups; one literal.

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: walk / dash max speed and acceleration

locations.note: walk cap 0x14C (0x1AC with unkC&0x40); flags&0x10 path uses 0x1DC/0x24C; accel 0x20/frame

items.notes: All Kirby movement constants are literals inside ~40 state functions (kirby.c lines 6000..16500), several duplicated per ability/medium (water, Mini, UFO). A 'kirby_physics' table is feasible but touches many sites; worth it only for a curated subset (walk, dash, jump, gravity, float).

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: jump impulse, gravity, terminal fall speed

locations.note: Macro_080435F8_3: other air state; water variant -8 / -0xE0

items.notes: Same constants repeated at many sites (e.g. -0x250 cap in ~15 places): first step would be named constants, then a table.

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: float (puffed) horizontal cap, flap lift, sink rate

locations.note: flap: +120 up to 0x150; sink -0x16 to -0x120; x cap 0x110

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: a few small motion curves are C tables
items.notes: gUnk_0834C160..gUnk_0834C5B7 (kirby.c:386..715): short velocity/offset curves. Already data-shaped.

items.subject: Kirby copy abilities
items.what: damage (unk63) and attack-kind bits (unk68) of each attack object

locations.note: Fighter 3 / Sword 4 / default 2 in one shared constructor
attack-kind bits select the element modifier column

items.notes: ~97 unk63 assignments in code_0806F780.c, one per attack object constructor (plus kirby.c). No per-ability stat table exists. A per-attack table keyed by constructor is possible but each constructor must be rewritten.

items.subject: Kirby copy abilities
items.what: projectile / dash speeds and lifetimes
items.notes: Literals inside each attack object's constructor/state; lifetimes are counter comparisons in the same functions.

items.subject: Kirby copy abilities
items.what: per-ability behaviour and animation tables
items.notes: Function-pointer tables are code, not tuning. The u8 ability lists and AnimInfo tables are data (gUnk_08350AAC/08350B30 HUD icons, gUnk_08D60FDC per-ability animation sets).

items.subject: Kirby
items.what: damage of the star spat after inhaling an object
items.notes: Derived from obj_desc.unk4 (hp): editing an enemy's hp also changes its star's power.

items.subject: food / items 0x5E..0x64
items.what: heal amount and rate
items.notes: Amount is in obj_desc; rate and the bonus roulette values (e.g. bonus.c:263 unkE2 = 1000) are literals.

items.subject: bosses / mini-bosses 0x38..0x52
items.what: starting hp by number of human players (1..4)
items.notes: ROM table at 0x08351530 (27 x 4 x s16), not yet a manifest kind: add 'boss_hp'. obj_desc.unk4 is ignored for these types. Rows 0x40..0x44 (empty types) are 2.

items.subject: Dark Mind form 1 (0x4F)
items.what: hp per encounter (placement subtype2 0..3) and player count

locations.note: forced to the last row when gUnk_0203AD10 & 4

items.notes: ROM table at 0x08351608, s16[8][4]: rows 0..3 are hp; rows 4..7 equal 0x4000/hp of rows 0..3 (a HUD scale like gUnk_08351458) but no reader of rows 4..7 was found.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: HUD hp-bar scale per boss and player count
items.notes: Every entry is floor(0x4000 / boss.hp) for the same cell (checked against the ROM). A mod that edits boss hp must regenerate it, or the bar will be wrong: make the pack compiler derive it.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: phase change at half hp (some bosses also at 1/4 and 3/4)

locations.note: subtype (placement subtype2) != 0 forces the second phase

items.notes: Derived from boss.hp (>>1, >>2) with the row index as a literal in each file. Quirk: dark_meta_knight.c uses row 0x10 (Gobbler's) for all its thresholds, not its own row 0x16 (the hp it starts with): editing DMK's hp does not move its phase points. Mr Frosty, Box Boxer and Crazy Hand have no hp-based phase; they only use subtype.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: attack choice odds, wind-up / cooldown timers, speeds
items.notes: Every boss file is a state machine with literal counters and RandLessThan / Rand16()&N odds (Dark Mind: ~100 Rand sites). Some movement is in motion-script tables (Kracko, Batafire, Gobbler, Bombar: see enemy.motion_scripts).

items.subject: bosses
items.what: song played when the fight starts
items.notes: Small C table; trivially data.

items.subject: bosses 0x43..0x52
items.what: what defeating a boss does (mirror shard drop, positions)
items.notes: Each handler hard-codes shard number and drop position (e.g. x=0x80, y=0x50). Progress logic, not tuning.

items.subject: boss attack objects
items.what: damage of boss projectiles/attacks
items.notes: As for enemies: per attack constructor. Nearly all are 1, so a per-type field would cover most of them.
